report.summary: Chunk 5 of 5 of canary.py: defines plan(), load_history(), append_history(), compare_to_history(), render_table(), and helpers.
risks: load_history | medium | silently drops corrupt lines; could mask data loss if filesystem corruption is frequent. | Check if silent drop is acceptable or if warning/logging is needed.

append_history | low | Uses `newline='
'` but writes `
`.join(lines) + '
'; on Windows this might produce double newlines or wrong line endings. | Verify behavior on Windows or if cross-platform support is intended.

compare_to_history | medium | `prior` filtering uses slicing [-window:] after list comprehension; if window > len(prior), returns all, but if window is negative? Not guarded. | Check if window is always positive; add guard if necessary.
render_table | low | Uses `_VERDICT` dict but does not handle missing keys; if a status not in dict appears, KeyError. | Ensure all possible statuses are covered or use .get().

handoff.purpose: Define plan() for dry-run plan, history functions, comparison logic, and table rendering.

symbols.name: plan
symbols.note: Returns a dict describing a dry-run plan; reads lanes, probes, and parameters.

symbols.name: load_history
symbols.note: Reads JSONL history file, skips unreadable lines, returns list of valid records.

symbols.name: append_history
symbols.note: Appends one JSONL line per probe result to history file; creates parent directories.

symbols.name: compare_to_history
symbols.note: Compares a ProbeResult against trailing history; returns Comparison with regression info.

symbols.name: _VERDICT
symbols.note: Mapping from status strings to short display labels.

symbols.name: _delta_cell
symbols.note: Formats delta_s for display; returns 'first' if first_ever, '-' if None, else signed float.

symbols.name: render_table
symbols.note: Renders a compact human-readable table from CanaryRun data.

claims.text: real payload rather than a guess about it.
claims.why: Refers to 'real payload' but no context; cannot verify against this chunk.

claims.text: ``live_seats`` states the PRICE: which lanes ``--live`` would actually call.
claims.why: In plan(), live_seats is set to list(live_egress_lanes(lanes)).

claims.text: A plan that shows the payload but not the bill is how ``--live`` becomes a surprise.
claims.why: Refers to --live behavior not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Naming a seat reads only its identity properties, which are pure.
claims.why: Refers to 'naming a seat' concept not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Read the JSONL history, SKIPPING anything unreadable.
claims.why: load_history uses try/except to skip lines that fail json.loads or are not dicts.

claims.text: A half-written last line (the machine was rebooted mid-append) must not take the health check down -- a canary that crashes on its own log is worse than no canary.
claims.why: load_history silently skips lines that raise ValueError/TypeError, so no crash.

claims.text: Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently and the rest of the file is still used.
claims.why: load_history checks record.get('schema') != SCHEMA_VERSION and skips them.

claims.text: Append one record per probe result. Parents created; never rewritten.
claims.why: append_history opens in append mode, creates parent dirs, writes lines.

claims.text: Latency and pass-rate against the trailing history for this triple.
claims.why: Function computes median latency and pass rate from history filtered by vendor/model/probe.

claims.text: ``previously_passed`` is "this exact vendor+model+probe has an ``ok`` on record".
claims.why: previously_passed = bool(oks) where oks are records with status 'ok'.

claims.text: That is what makes ``regressed`` mean "it used to work and now it does not" rather than "it is red", and it is why a lane that has never passed cannot page anyone: there is no evidence it ever could.
claims.why: regressed = previously_passed and result.status in FAILING_STATUSES.

claims.text: An ``unavailable`` result is NEVER a regression. We did not ask, so nothing regressed -- the bench being asleep is not the bench being broken.
claims.why: regression only checks result.status in FAILING_STATUSES; unavailable is not in FAILING_STATUSES (assumed).

claims.text: Compact human table: vendor, model, probe verdict, latency, vs median.
claims.why: render_table produces table with those columns.

observations.what: load_history silently drops lines that are not valid JSON or not dicts or wrong schema. No logging of dropped lines.

append_history opens file with newline='
' but writes '
'.join(lines) + '
'. On Windows, this may produce extra carriage returns.
compare_to_history uses list comprehension then slices [-window:] without checking window is positive; if window is 0 or negative, behavior is questionable.
_VERDICT dict does not include all possible statuses; if a status not in dict is passed, KeyError will occur.
